title: Vertiv Power Innovation Day 2026: The macro forces shaping data center power in 2026
summary: Learn how higher-voltage DC architectures, modular deployment, and collaboration are solving AI data center power challenges.
body_text: The first episode of Vertiv Power Innovation Day 2026 brings together Kyle Keeper , Senior Vice President of Power Management at Vertiv, and Phillip Marangella , Chief Marketing and Product Officer, EdgeConneX, in a conversation hosted by Stephen Worn , Chief Technology Officer and Managing Director, Datacenter Dynamics (DCD). They discuss the voltage and density changes reshaping rack-level power delivery, what infrastructure planning now demands, and how the industry is responding through partnership and collaboration. Stephen Worn, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and Managing Director, DatacenterDynamics (DCD): The scale of secure power demand has radically changed. What macro forces are driving this? Phillip Marangella, Chief Marketing & Product Officer, EdgeConneX: When we started out, these "edge" data centers were one to two megawatts. Now, those are just racks. What’s driving the shift is no longer just about getting power to the data center, but also to the rack— at scale and at speed. Deployments used to take 24–36 months, but now customers want them in 12-18 months. This requires being flexible to customer requirements and scalable as you move to next-generation chipsets, so we can support new workloads without a major retrofit. Kyle Keeper, Senior Vice President of Power Management, Vertiv: The challenge goes beyond the sheer power demand from AI factories—it extends to the dynamic nature and type of loads that must be supported. That includes addressing rising power densities at the row and rack level and rethinking power strategies to handle power availability and grid dynamics. The question is how to plan for a deployment today while staying ready for what's still to come. Stephen: You have visibility across utilities, hyperscalers, operators, and end users. How is Vertiv responding? Kyle: That's not how this industry always worked. The challenges are creating collaboration and early engagement—with regulatory bodies, governments, and municipalities—around grid regulations and even noise ordinances. Our focus is on what is ready now: how do we deliver power from the site to the rack, safely, efficiently, and without designing ourselves into a corner? We see data centers evolving from passive loads to grid-enhancing assets. We’re also headed towards flexibility and hybrid architectures or higher-voltage AC and DC power, on-site generation, and grid-interactive control schemes. Stephen: Rack density is pushing voltage requirements from 415V AC toward 800V DC. How is that changing how power gets to the rack? Phillip: The technology is evolving faster than operations can keep up. The shift to liquid cooling is one example; operational teams are being asked to handle something that used to be taboo in data centers, and it requires rewriting operational procedures. Power is no different: with grid constraints and availability, you're always looking at alternative solutions to deliver the capacity when it's needed. Whether it's on-site natural gas , behind-the-meter, or battery energy storage systems (BESS) , these are all in the quiver to augment supply. Kyle: The industry has come to terms with higher voltages . Hybrid architectures with AC and DC already exist today. DC already exists at the rack level. A long time ago, DC power moved out of the server into the rack, and that's not going away. We see existing platforms around 54-volt DC continuing to support upcoming generations of graphics processing unit (GPU) servers. We'll also see a transition to 100-volt systems with sidecar approaches. This approach helps support higher density in the rack and simplifies power distribution to the GPU pod. Stephen: What you build today has to support chip generations not yet available. How does Vertiv plan for that from a roadmap perspective? Kyle: We've gone from an era where the power system just worked to one where it should be viewed as a strategic platform for data center designers and operators. We're not designing for a single point in time but for a series of future design points. One of the biggest concerns is designing and deploying with greater certainty: certainty in timing, certainty in how solutions can be deployed, and certainty in how they will perform. If you take two sites of the same size, there is an ability to differentiate based on system design: how it's architected, deployed, and operated over time. Thinking through phased energization, how systems perform under these workloads, and how they interconnect with the grid — these factors create real differences. In spite of the complexity, it's manageable. We're already in a phase of real-world deployments. Stephen: The scale demands power and cooling solutions that work together. How do you deliver that on time, on budget? Kyle: We've designed against this idea of repeatable building blocks. The question is whether we can do it at scale: pre-engineered, prefabricated, validated, in a more factory environment . The more we can do as an industry in that fashion versus bespoke on-site work using generalist resources that might be seeing this equipment for the first time — that is a risky way of going about this. Efficiency and optimization haven't gone away, but more predictable deployments, being able to do it at speed, at scale — those are the models that are going to be most successful. Stephen: Predictable deployment at speed and scale. How can we succeed with you? Phillip: We are succeeding. You reduce risk with communication, collaboration, and partnership. We see power as an impediment. We're going to solve for it, and it's going to improve the overall grid architecture as a result. That has been underappreciated over the years. It's going to be good for the entire power ecosystem. Buckle up. Because as fast as we've been going, it's only going to get faster. You've got to be brave, you've got to be patient. But it's fun. We're on this rocket ship. Kyle: The ones that are most successful are going to be those that have the strongest partnerships. We value partnerships like those with EdgeConneX — you make us smarter. We're going to have to continue to get smarter. We're proud of our heritage, but we have to continue to evolve. We're well positioned for what's needed today and what's yet to come. Watch the full conversation: The macro forces shaping data center power in 2026

title: Best Coda Alternatives: 8 Tools Compared for Teams in 2026
summary: If you're evaluating Coda alternatives, you've likely hit one of three walls: the learning curve is steeper than your team can absorb, the free plan's row limits are choking your data, or you need stronger capabilities in a specific area - whether that's project management, structured data, or building internal
body_text: If you're evaluating Coda alternatives, you've likely hit one of three walls: the learning curve is steeper than your team can absorb, the free plan's row limits are choking your data, or you need stronger capabilities in a specific area - whether that's project management, structured data, or building internal tools. Coda combines document editing, spreadsheets, and database functionality into a single app, and that flexibility is genuinely hard to replicate. But specialized tools often outperform it in the areas that matter most to your team. The short answer: No single alternative replaces everything Coda does. But for most teams, a focused tool delivers better results. Choose Notion if documentation and knowledge management drive your work. Choose Airtable if structured data management is your priority. Choose Jet Admin or Retool if you need to build internal business applications on existing databases. The right Coda alternative depends on your team size, technical skill level, and whether your workflows are document-first, data-first, or tool-first. What Is Coda? Coda is a connected workspace that merges documents, relational databases, and application logic into a single surface. Its formula language supports row-level logic, cross-table lookups, and embedded actions like buttons that trigger automations - making it a spreadsheet database hybrid that can function as a lightweight app builder. Typical use cases include interactive project trackers, operational dashboards built inside documents, and workflow automation through its "Packs" integration system. The trade-offs are real, though. Coda's free plan caps usage at roughly 1,000 rows across all tables in a document and 50 objects per doc. Performance degrades noticeably in large, formula-heavy documents. And the doc maker pricing model - while potentially cost-effective when most users are editors or viewers - means paid plans can reach approximately $36/user/month at the Team tier, which is significantly higher than several alternatives. How to Evaluate Coda Alternatives: Key Decision Criteria Before diving into specific tools, establish what matters for your team. Coda alternatives vary based on priorities like document collaboration, relational databases, and project management, so aligning on criteria prevents expensive tool switches later. Build speed - How quickly can your team ship functional workflows, dashboards, or documents? Template availability, UI intuitiveness, and onboarding friction all factor in. Data connectivity - Native connectors to databases, SaaS tools, and APIs. Does the tool support webhooks, live sync, or two-way data flows with your existing stack? Extensibility and automation - Can you automate workflows with formulas, rules, scripting, or custom logic? How sophisticated can triggers and actions get? Authentication and permissions - User roles, granular access controls, guest access, and the distinction between creators and viewers. This directly affects both security and cost. Deployment options - Cloud-only versus on-premises, VPC, or hybrid. Mobile app quality and offline support matter for distributed teams. Governance - Audit trails, version history, compliance certifications (SOC 2, data residency), and administrative controls for enterprise environments. Pricing model - Per-seat, per-creator, or usage-based pricing. Free tier generosity. How total cost of ownership scales as your team grows. Maintenance requirements - Setup complexity, required training investment, ongoing administration, and technical support quality. Coda Alternatives: Quick Comparison Table Alternative Best For Starting Price Deployment Learning Curve Notion Knowledge management, team wikis Free; paid plans start ~$12/user/mo Cloud, desktop, mobile Low Airtable Structured data, relational databases Free; paid ~$20/user/mo Cloud, mobile Low–Medium ClickUp Full-scale project management Free; paid ~$7/user/mo Cloud, desktop, mobile Medium Fibery Complex interconnected workflows ~$20/user/mo Cloud Medium–High Monday.com Visual project tracking ~$12/seat/mo (min 3 seats) Cloud, mobile Low–Medium Basecamp Simple team collaboration Flat-rate ~$349/mo unlimited users Cloud, mobile Very Low Jet Admin Custom business applications See Jet Admin pricing Cloud, custom domains Medium Retool Developer-centric internal tools Free; enterprise pricing varies Cloud, self-hosted High The key trade-off: tools that match Coda's flexibility (Fibery, Retool) demand more technical skill, while tools that are easier to adopt (Notion, Basecamp) sacrifice depth in automation or data modeling. Notion: Best for Knowledge Management and Team Wikis Notion is a block-based workspace that merges documents, task tracking, and databases into a flexible workspace that millions of teams use daily. Notion is a leading Coda alternative for documentation, and it's the tool most teams evaluate first when moving away from Coda. Best for: Documentation-heavy teams, personal productivity, personal knowledge bases and team wikis. Choose Notion if your primary workflow involves note taking, meeting notes, long documents, knowledge bases, and light project coordination. Strengths: Notion's interface is cleaner and more intuitive than Coda's, with a polished block-based editor that makes creating team wikis and knowledge bases fast. Notion is easier to use than Coda for basic workflows. Notion has over 10,000 templates available for users, covering everything from project dashboards to personal productivity systems - dramatically reducing build speed. The free tier is genuinely generous: unlimited pages and blocks, guest access, and basic version history. For non-technical users and small teams, this alone makes it compelling. AI features including Notion Agents for content generation, PDF/image processing, and natural-language database creation add value on paid plans. Notion is best for personal knowledge bases and team wikis. Limitations: Formula and relational database power are notably weaker than Coda's. Cross-document computation is constrained, and you can't embed interactive actions (buttons triggering logic) inside documents the way Coda allows. Native automations are simpler - fewer triggers, fewer action types, and no equivalent to Coda's Packs for two-way live data sync with external tools. Every user generally needs a paid seat for full access. There's no doc maker versus editor distinction, which means scaling can get expensive when many users only need to view or lightly edit. Offline mode and mobile experience are improving but still limited for power users; performance can degrade with extremely large databases. Pricing: Free plan with generous content limits. Plus tier around $12/user/month; Business tier approximately $18/user/month (annual billing). Significantly less expensive per user than Coda's Team tier for most team structures. Airtable: Best for Structured Data and Database Management Airtable is a spreadsheet-database hybrid for structured data management, and it's the best coda alternative for teams whose work revolves around organizing, filtering, and visualizing data in structured formats. Airtable excels in structured data management compared to Coda, particularly when you need rich field types and multiple ways to visualize data. Best for: Teams managing structured data like inventories, CRM pipelines, content calendars, and operational workflows. Airtable is ideal for managing structured data and relational databases. Strengths: Airtable offers 14+ view types including Gantt and Map views - far more than Coda's view options. Grid, gallery, calendar, kanban, timeline, and custom views give teams flexibility to track work exactly how they need to. The data-first approach with strong relational tables, forms for data input, and a robust API makes it excellent for database-driven workflows. Airtable is better for structured data management than Coda. Automations and scripting blocks enable meaningful business logic. Integration ecosystem is well-developed with native connectors to major SaaS tools. Performance with moderately large datasets (hundreds to thousands of records) is solid and predictable. Limitations: Document-centric or narrative content is secondary. You can't build long documents with embedded interactive components the way you can in Coda docs. Interface builder capabilities for custom front-end experiences are more limited unless you pair Airtable with other tools. Pricing can be steep: the entry paid plan starts around $20/user/month. For teams with many users, total cost of ownership climbs quickly. Performance degrades with very large bases or deeply nested relational structures - users report view lagging and slow filtering at scale. Pricing: Free tier with limited records. Paid plans start at approximately $20/user/month. According to ITQlick's 2026 comparison , Airtable scored 95/100 versus Coda's 82/100, with higher user ratings for value-for-money in typical business use cases. ClickUp: Best for Comprehensive Project Management ClickUp is a comprehensive work management platform designed to replace multiple tools with a single unified workspace. ClickUp offers built-in project management features without setup - task lists, time tracking, project dashboards, docs, and team communication come included out of the box. ClickUp has built-in project management features without custom setup. Best for: Teams needing full-scale project management capabilities with minimal configuration. ClickUp combines tasks, docs, goals, and team dashboards in one workspace. Strengths: Complete PM feature set including task management, time tracking, project discussions, file sharing, custom views, and team messaging - all native, no Packs or integrations required. Affordable pricing with a meaningful free plan and paid plans starting around $7/user/month, making it one of the most cost-effective options for growing teams. Quick deployment: most teams can get productive within days rather than weeks. Templates and pre-built project trackers reduce setup time. Strong mobile experience compared to Coda, with functional apps for iOS and Android. Limitations: The sheer volume of features creates its own complexity. New users often report feeling overwhelmed by the interface, and customization options - while extensive - can lead to configuration sprawl. Less flexible than Coda for custom workflows that blend documents, databases, and application logic. ClickUp's docs and databases exist as separate features rather than a truly connected workspace. Formula and relational data capabilities are basic compared to Coda or Airtable. Teams with data-heavy analytical workflows may find it insufficient. Performance can slow with very large workspaces or heavily customized views. Pricing: Free plan available. Paid plans start at approximately $7/user/month (annual billing), making it among the most affordable options for project management teams. Fibery: Best for Complex, Interconnected Workflows Fibery integrates relational databases with documentation and workflows in a way that appeals to product teams, agencies, and organizations modeling complex systems. Unlike Coda's document-with-tables approach, Fibery uses a "connected spaces" architecture where entities, relations, and workflows are first-class concepts. Fibery allows for flexible workflows and deep data relationships. Best for: Product teams and agencies needing deeply connected data relationships, software-process modeling, roadmaps, and internal productivity platforms. Fibery integrates relational databases and documentation for project management. Strengths: Advanced data modeling with spaces, entities, and relations that mirror how software teams actually think about their work. Less reliance on workarounds compared to building similar structures in Coda. Visual whiteboard views, flexible field types, built-in automations and rules, and an AI setup assistant that helps configure workspaces for specific use cases. Observer/guest pricing means you're not paying full seat costs for stakeholders who only need to view data - a significant advantage over tools that charge per user regardless of role. Cleaner entity modeling than Coda, according to users who've migrated between the two platforms. Reddit discussions frequently cite better design and less workaround-heavy workflows. Limitations: Steep learning curve: modeling spaces, relations, and automations requires meaningful investment. Non-technical users may struggle without dedicated onboarding. Mobile experience is weaker - the mobile app is underdeveloped compared to Notion or ClickUp, and mobile web performance is subpar. Smaller template ecosystem and community compared to Notion or Airtable. Fewer out-of-the-box examples for teams that want to start quickly. Pricing starts around $20/user/month and increases for advanced relational and permission features. Pricing: Starting at approximately $20/user/month. Advanced features and role-based permissions incur additional costs. Observer/guest pricing helps control costs for larger organizations with many view-only stakeholders. Monday.com: Best for Visual Project Tracking Monday.com focuses on visual tracking and no-code automation for project management, serving teams that prefer color-coded boards and intuitive drag-and-drop interfaces over formula-driven workflows. Monday.com serves over 1 billion dollars in revenue globally, reflecting its established position as a visual project tracking platform. Best for: Teams preferring visual, color-coded project boards with strong automation capabilities. Ideal for marketing teams, operations groups, and cross-functional project coordination. Strengths: Intuitive visual interface with color coded boards that make project status immediately clear. Non-technical users can get productive quickly without training. Strong automation builder with no-code triggers and actions. Teams can automate workflows for notifications, status changes, assignments, and integrations without writing formulas. Established platform with extensive marketplace integrations, a mature mobile app, and reliable performance at scale. Multiple view types including Gantt, timeline, kanban, and team dashboards provide flexibility for visual project management. Limitations: Less database flexibility than Coda or Airtable. Monday.com's data model is board-centric rather than relationally structured, which limits complex data relationships. Higher costs at scale: pricing starts around $12/seat/month with a minimum of 3 seats, and advanced features (private boards, time tracking, formula columns) require higher tiers. Customization depth is limited compared to Coda's formula-driven approach. Teams needing highly custom workflows may find the platform constraining. The platform is optimized for project management workflows; using it as a general-purpose database or document editor pushes against its design intent. Pricing: Paid plans start at approximately $12/seat/month (minimum 3 seats). Pro and Enterprise tiers unlock advanced automations, integrations, and governance features at higher per-seat costs. Basecamp: Best for Simple Team Collaboration Basecamp simplifies project collaboration with minimal configuration, taking the opposite approach from Coda's build-anything philosophy. Basecamp focuses on simple project collaboration without complex setup - it provides a fixed set of tools (message boards, to-dos, schedules, file sharing, campfire chat) and deliberately avoids customization complexity. Best for: Small teams wanting straightforward project coordination without the overhead of configuring custom workflows or learning complex systems. Strengths: Simplicity is the product. Message boards, task lists, project discussions, and file sharing work reliably without configuration. New users can be productive within minutes. Flat-rate pricing at approximately $349/month for unlimited users eliminates per-seat cost anxiety. For teams larger than ~25 people, this becomes significantly cheaper than per-user alternatives. Proven track record over two decades. The team communication model (campfire chat, project discussions, automatic check-ins) reduces meeting load. Basecamp simplifies project coordination compared to Coda - there's nothing to misconfigure because there's little to configure. Limitations: No database features, no relational data, no formulas, no custom views. If your workflow requires any form of structured data management, Basecamp simply doesn't address it. Limited customization means teams outgrow it as complexity increases. No custom workflows, no automation beyond basic notifications. No Gantt charts, no time tracking, no advanced project dashboards. Teams needing visual project tracking or detailed reporting need additional tools. Integration ecosystem is minimal compared to Coda, Notion, or Airtable. Pricing: Flat-rate ~$349/month for unlimited users, or a free personal tier with limited projects. The unlimited users model makes it uniquely cost-effective for larger simple-collaboration teams. Jet Admin: Best for Building Custom Business Applications Jet Admin builds secure business apps on existing data - it generates the interface and application/backend logic, then deploys the app to users. Where Coda embeds lightweight app behavior inside documents, Jet Admin produces standalone business applications with custom domains, user authentication, and governed data access. Best for: Teams needing to build internal tools, admin panels, and custom business applications on top of existing databases and APIs without full engineering cycles. Strengths: Connects to existing databases, APIs, spreadsheets, and SaaS tools through an extensive integrations catalog . Supported databases include PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Firebase/Firestore, Supabase, and many more. SaaS connectors cover Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Shopify, Jira, and dozens of others. Visual builder for CRUD operations, dashboards, KPI displays with chart components, and data export (CSV, Excel, JSON, PDF). Custom actions ("Flex Actions") enable embedding business logic via API. Supports custom domains and deployment configurations, giving teams control over how applications are presented to end users. Storage connectors including Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, and authentication options (Google OAuth, OIDC, Auth0) provide enterprise-grade infrastructure. Limitations: Focused on app building rather than documentation or narrative content. If your team needs team wikis, knowledge bases, or long documents, Jet Admin isn't designed for that. Requires existing data sources - it builds on your databases and APIs, not as a standalone data store like Airtable or Coda. Teams accustomed to Coda's document-centric workflow will find the paradigm different: Jet Admin produces applications, not interactive documents. Pricing: See the Jet Admin pricing page for current plans and tiers. Retool: Best for Developer-Friendly Internal Tools Retool occupies similar territory to Jet Admin but skews more toward developer-centric teams who want code-level control. It provides drag-and-drop UI components (tables, forms, charts) with the ability to drop into JavaScript for custom logic, making it powerful for complex internal applications. Best for: Technical teams building complex internal applications - admin panels, support ops UIs, data pipelines - where governance, security, and custom logic are priorities. Strengths: Powerful component library with drag-and-drop UI building plus JavaScript support for custom logic. Teams can embed custom React components when standard components aren't sufficient. Extensive integrations with databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and more), REST/GraphQL APIs, and SaaS tools. Connectors are robust and well-documented. Enterprise-ready features: role-based access controls, audit trails, SSO, and self-hosted deployment options for teams with strict governance requirements. Fast initial build speed for CRUD interfaces, dashboards, and admin tools - Retool's documentation highlights rapid internal tool development as a core value. Limitations: Requires technical skills. Non-developer teams will struggle to build or maintain complex workflows. The learning curve is steep for anyone without JavaScript familiarity. Not document-oriented. Building narrative content, combining prose with data and formulas inside a document, or creating knowledge bases requires combining Retool with other tools. "Maintenance debt" is a real concern: users on Reddit caution that initial build speed is high, but ongoing permission tweaks, UI changes, and connector maintenance consume engineering time. Desktop-first focus. Mobile support exists but isn't optimized for field usage or mobile-heavy workflows. Pricing: Free tier available for small teams. Per-user pricing increases with enterprise features (self-hosting, audit logs, SSO). Total cost of ownership rises with user count and application complexity. Which Coda Alternative Should You Choose? Choose Notion if your team prioritizes documentation, knowledge management, and team wikis over complex databases. Notion is popular for personal knowledge management and team wikis, and its generous free tier makes it the easiest starting point. Choose Airtable if structured data and relational databases are your primary need. Its 14+ view types and data-first approach outperform Coda for inventory, CRM, and pipeline workflows. Choose ClickUp if you want comprehensive project management features - task lists, time tracking, team dashboards - with minimal setup and affordable per-user pricing. Choose Jet Admin if you need to build custom business applications on existing databases and APIs. It generates secure, deployable apps with governed data access - a fundamentally different approach from Coda's document-embedded logic. Choose Fibery if you require complex, interconnected workflows with deep customization and are willing to invest in configuration time. Choose Monday.com if your team prefers visual project tracking with color-coded boards and no-code automation, and project management is the primary use case. Choose Basecamp if you want simple team collaboration with flat-rate pricing and zero configuration overhead. Stay with Coda if your team has mastered its formula system and genuinely needs its unique document-database hybrid approach - interactive documents with embedded buttons, cross-table logic, and live data Packs. Migration and Selection Checklist Before committing to any alternative: Audit current Coda usage - Count your documents, tables, automations, integrations, and the number of doc makers versus editors/viewers. Identify power users - Determine who relies on Coda's formula features, embedded buttons, cross-table logic, and Pack integrations. Their requirements are the hardest to migrate. Test with real data - Prototype your most critical workflows in candidate tools using actual data, not demos. Evaluate how relational joins, formulas, and embedded logic perform under realistic conditions. Evaluate migration effort - Which tools offer CSV or API import from Coda? Which require manual rebuilding of automations and logic? Factor this into your timeline. Consider training requirements - Tools like Fibery and Retool require more upfront investment in learning. Budget for onboarding time and change management. Calculate total cost of ownership over 2–3 years - Include seat costs, admin overhead, performance-related costs, data storage, backup/export capabilities, and governance features. A tool that's cheaper per seat but requires more engineering maintenance may cost more overall. Recommendations by Team Type and Technical Skill Team Profile Recommended Tools Non-technical small teams (under 10) Basecamp or Notion Growing teams needing project management ClickUp or Monday.com Data-heavy organizations Airtable or Fibery Technical teams building internal tools Jet Admin or Retool Enterprise teams with governance needs Fibery, Retool (self-hosted), or Jet Admin Hybrid doc-and-data workflows Stay with Coda or combine Notion + Airtable Frequently Asked Questions What is the closest free alternative to Coda? Notion offers the most generous free plan among Coda alternatives: unlimited pages and blocks, guest access, and basic version history - with no row limits on content. Coda's free plan caps you at roughly 1,000 rows across all tables and 50 objects per document. ClickUp also offers a meaningful free tier with task management, docs, and limited storage. Supernotes offers a free plan with 100 cards to start for teams focused specifically on fast, focused note-taking with real-time collaboration. Grist offers strict data typing to prevent formula errors in knowledge management and has an open-source self-hosted option. Can I migrate my existing Coda docs to these alternatives? Migration complexity varies significantly. Notion and Airtable support CSV imports, so tabular data transfers relatively smoothly. Automations, embedded buttons, and Pack integrations have no direct migration path - these require manual rebuilding in any alternative. Fibery offers import capabilities for structured data but requires reconfiguring entity relationships. For Retool and Jet Admin, migration is less about importing Coda content and more about connecting to your underlying data sources directly. Plan for a phased migration rather than a one-time switch. Which alternative handles complex formulas and automation best? No alternative exactly replicates Coda's formula system, which allows row-level logic, cross-table lookups, and formula-triggered actions embedded in documents. Airtable's scripting blocks and automations handle substantial business logic for structured data workflows. Fibery's rules and automations support complex interconnected workflows. ClickUp's automations are practical for project management triggers but less flexible for data manipulation. Grist enforces strict data typing to prevent formula errors, which can actually be an advantage - it catches mistakes that Coda's more permissive system allows through. Supernotes uses small, structured note cards for quick idea capture, which is a fundamentally different paradigm from formula-driven workflows. What's the most cost-effective Coda alternative for growing teams? For teams under 25 people, ClickUp (starting ~$7/user/month) or Notion (~$12/user/month) typically offer the best value. For teams over 25 where most users are non-technical, Basecamp's flat-rate ~$349/month for unlimited users becomes very competitive. Coda's doc maker pricing model can work in your favor if only a few team members create content and most are editors/viewers, but the ~$36/user/month Team tier is expensive when compared to alternatives. Calculate your specific ratio of creators to viewers before deciding. Do any alternatives offer better mobile experiences than Coda? Yes. Notion and ClickUp both offer more polished mobile apps than Coda, with functional offline support and responsive interfaces. Monday.com's mobile app is well-regarded for visual project tracking on the go. Basecamp's mobile app is straightforward and reliable for team messaging and project discussions. Fibery's mobile experience is weaker - users consistently report it as underdeveloped. Retool and Jet Admin are primarily desktop-first, though both render in mobile browsers. Supernotes is designed for fast, focused note-taking with real-time collaboration and works well on mobile for its specific use case. Which tool is best for teams already using Google Workspace or Microsoft 365? Notion integrates well with Google Workspace for embedding Google Docs, Sheets, and Calendar. Airtable connects to Google Sheets and offers strong API-based integrations with both ecosystems. ClickUp and Monday.com both offer native integrations with Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 for calendar sync, file sharing, and email notifications. Jet Admin connects to Google Sheets and Google Docs natively, plus supports Google OAuth for authentication - making it practical for teams building internal tools within a Google Workspace environment. Slite is designed for creating and organizing internal documents and knowledge, and integrates with both Google and Microsoft ecosystems for document-heavy teams. Looking to build internal tools and business applications on your existing data? Explore Jet Admin's integrations to see how it connects to your databases, APIs, and SaaS tools - and start building without writing code from scratch.

body_text: View All News MindWalk Showcases ReefIQ™ for AI Drug Discovery at AMD Advancing AI July 23, 2026 At Advancing AI 2026, MindWalk unveils the first public demonstration of ReefIQ, its biological context layer for AI drug discovery, running on AMD Instinct™. AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- MindWalk Holdings Corp. (“MindWalk”) (NASDAQ: HYFT), a Bio-Native AI company, today unveiled the first public demonstration of ReefIQ™, its biological context layer for AI drug discovery, running on AMD Instinct™ at AMD’s Advancing AI 2026 in San Francisco. MindWalk is featured in the AMD Instinct™ Demo Showcase, appearing in one of four custom demo vignettes, with an accompanying video interview distributed through AMD’s channels. The demonstration is the first time MindWalk has shown ReefIQ publicly in action. It walks through how ReefIQ reconnects fragmented discovery data into governed, queryable biological context, then lets AI models and agents reason over that context, running on open AMD Instinct compute. ReefIQ, which MindWalk introduced in June 2026, sits between client discovery data and AI reasoning workflows. A brand film introducing ReefIQ is available at: https://youtu.be/S5kVmpc-ik4 What ReefIQ is Biology is connected, but drug-discovery data is often fragmented across files, formats, systems, teams, and workflows. ReefIQ reconnects those representations before AI workflows act on them. Sequences, structures, assay outputs, omics, literature, evidence, provenance, and program history become governed, queryable connected biological context for AI-enabled discovery. HYFT® Technology is MindWalk’s core biological pattern technology, the biological representation foundation with explicit relationships across sequence, structure, function, mechanism, pathway, evidence, and literature. ReefIQ™ is the client biological context layer built on HYFT. LensAI™ is the reasoning and application layer. HYFT powers the biological representation. ReefIQ organizes and governs the context. LensAI applies reasoning workflows. “In life-sciences AI, the durable advantage is not the model a team licenses but the biological context it can reason over. Biology is connected by evolutionary constraint; discovery data arrives fragmented across files and systems, and that gap is where insight is lost. ReefIQ is designed to close it, preserving what every program learns, including the programs that fail, as governed context rather than isolated files. In a regulated setting, that is what makes reasoning trustworthy, and trustworthy is what compounds into the clinic,” said Dr. Jennifer Bath, PhD, CEO and President of MindWalk Holdings Corp. Why it matters Drug-discovery organizations generate valuable context in every program: positive results, negative results, assay conditions, design decisions, mechanism hypotheses, literature links, and the reasons candidates did not advance. ReefIQ preserves that context as governed, queryable knowledge. As data are added, the network is enriched and its relationships and annotations are refined. Future programs benefit from the ever-compounding evidence and insights. HYFT reasoning is grounded in evolutionary constraint, the patterns biology preserves because their function is non-negotiable, rather than statistical correlation. In regulated drug discovery, where a hallucinated result is a patient-safety and program-cost problem, that grounding is what makes reasoning, including autonomous and agentic reasoning, trustworthy enough to act on. Why AMD Instinct Bio-Native inference is data-dominated and memory-heavy: enrichment, similarity search across hundreds of millions of patterns, and reasoning over connected biological context. AMD Instinct’s memory-rich, open-stack, portable profile maps onto that workload. The architecture supports flexible integration across data governance, model access, and compute deployment, so a customer’s connected context stays in the customer’s environment under existing governance while inference runs on open compute. “ReefIQ operationalizes the HYFT information network for drug discovery,” said Dirk Van Hyfte, MD, PhD, Chief Technology Officer of MindWalk AI. “HYFT provides the biological representation foundation, representing the complex relationships in biology; ReefIQ links customer data to that foundation and exposes governed context to LensAI and customer-selected agent models operating within agreed governance. The goal is to support retrieval, analysis, and hypothesis generation over connected biological context while preserving provenance, deployment flexibility, and customer-defined controls.” What comes next MindWalk’s Business Development team will use Advancing AI 2026 to engage life-sciences customers, infrastructure partners, and agentic-AI builders evaluating where to host and govern regulated biological context. LensAI is already in contracted, recurring arrangements with life-sciences customers today. Interested parties may request a private briefing through Investor Relations. For more information about the technology, visit https://www.mindwalkai.com/reefiq . About MindWalk Holdings Corp. MindWalk Holdings Corp. (NASDAQ: HYFT) is a Bio-Native AI company building the BioIntelligence infrastructure that life sciences AI and agentic AI require. Its proprietary HYFT® Technology powers ReefIQ™, the biological context layer for life sciences, organized around function-aware HYFT pattern-objects that span sequence and structural biology and refined over 20 years of curation across a continuously evolving biological representation of 660 million biological patterns and 25 billion relationships, that enriches data at ingestion and compounds in analytical value with every program run on the platform. The LensAI platform operates on this infrastructure to enable target discovery, candidate diligence, and portfolio decision support, and to host the agentic AI workflows pharma is racing to deploy. MindWalk’s architecture is designed so that the HYFT representation layer, not any individual AI model, is the durable, compounding competitive asset. title: Why USPS is betting big on the future of mail
summary: Why USPS is betting big on the future of mail: USPS's Steve Mills on billion-dollar investments, mailer promotions, and why direct mail ROI keeps growing.
body_text: Mail isn’t going anywhere. For more than 250 years, the Postal Service has connected people, businesses, and communities across the United States and the world. USPS’s relevance transcends technology and trends. Long before cars, planes, and the Internet existed, USPS pioneered our country’s first communication channel. Today, it delivers roughly 40% of the world’s mail volume – processing and delivering billions of mail pieces each year through an increasingly sophisticated ecosystem of infrastructure, logistics, and technology. USPS has continually evolved, embracing new technologies and innovations, such as zip codes, automated sorting, and barcode scanning, to reach its ever-expanding delivery network. Modern direct mail is more dynamic and data-driven than ever before. Its advanced personalization, integration, and automation capabilities blur the lines between physical and digital channels . With a response rate of approximately 15%, no other marketing channel drives action and engagement like direct mail. As part of our Postal Fix series, we recently sat down with Steve Mills, Director of Product Management, Mailing Services at USPS for exclusive insights on the enduring value of direct mail and what the future may hold. Watch the full Fireside Chat here . How USPS is reimagining mail “Physical mail still connects with people,” says Mills. “It still has pretty much one of the highest return on ad spend (ROAS) and total return on investment (ROI) of any channel. And that’s why I think mail is always going to be relevant. Now it’s a matter of how to keep it as relevant, targeted, and useful to the end user as possible.” To understand where mail is headed, look where USPS is investing: technology, facilities, programs, and other new ways to drive long-term mail performance. “We’re investing a billion dollars back into the industry every year to keep mail relevant, and to help the whole ecosystem, the whole industry, grow,” says Mills. For example, the latest USPS promotions and incentives encourage mailers to use features that make mail more relevant and engaging, with discounts between 3% and 7%. The Mail Growth Incentive gives $500 million per year back to the industry. Those like the Integrated Technology promotion and the Tactile, Sensory, & Interactive promotion reward mailers who incorporate augmented reality, tactile treatments, multisensory elements, and other innovative concepts. How to be a part of the future of mail The future of mail is already here. And it’s shaped by the people and organizations who use it every day. “We all need to work together to make sure that mail stays effective and people are making the changes they need to make to keep mail relevant and the industry vibrant,” says Mills. Stay involved, he recommends. Your voice matters. Join industry associations. Talk to your mail service providers . Connect with industry peers. The most successful teams won’t just wait and see, they’re the ones already evolving with the new mail ecosystem. Mail has always been about connection. That’s not going to change. While mail volumes ebb and flow, the volume of targeted, personalized mail continues to grow steadily. People respond to relevance. They always have. The future of mail is still being written Explore more Postal Fix articles, expert interviews, and USPS insights to stay ahead of industry changes and make the most of your direct mail programs . Visit lob.com/postalfix to read the full series.

title: Best Construction Payroll Software in 2026: The Complete Buyer's Guide for Specialty Trade Contractors
summary: A buyer's guide to construction payroll software for specialty contractors, covering prevailing wage, union logic, certified payroll, and what to evaluate.
body_text: Payroll in construction is fundamentally different from payroll in every other industry. A single pay period can involve workers across multiple states, trade classifications that determine different hourly rates, prevailing wage determinations that vary by project, union overtime rules that differ from federal standards, and fringe benefit obligations that must be calculated and reported separately on certified payroll filings. General-purpose payroll software was not built for any of that. For specialty trade contractors evaluating payroll platforms in 2026, the question is not which software has the most features. The question is which platform handles the specific complexity that construction payroll demands, without requiring the back-office team to compensate for what the software cannot do. Here is what to look for, where most platforms fall short, and how to evaluate your options based on how your operation actually runs. What Construction Payroll Software Needs to Handle Before comparing platforms, contractors need a clear picture of what construction payroll actually requires. The gap between what general payroll tools offer and what construction demands is where most buying mistakes happen. Prevailing Wage and Davis-Bacon Compliance On federally funded projects subject to the Davis-Bacon Act, contractors must pay workers at least the prevailing wage rate for their trade classification in the project's geographic area. The prevailing wage consists of a basic hourly rate plus a fringe benefit rate. Payroll software for contractors working on these projects must apply the correct wage determination, calculate fringe benefits accurately, and produce certified payroll reports (Form WH-347) that reflect the correct rates, hours, and classifications for each worker every week. State prevailing wage laws add another layer. Many states have their own prevailing wage requirements with different rate structures, reporting formats, and filing deadlines. A platform that handles federal prevailing wage but not state-level requirements leaves a gap that the admin team fills manually. Union Payroll Logic Union contractors face payroll rules that vary by trade, local, and collective bargaining agreement. Different overtime triggers, benefit fund contribution rates, dues calculations, and reporting requirements can apply to different workers on the same jobsite. Payroll software that treats union logic as an edge case or requires manual overrides for every union-specific calculation creates a recurring compliance risk every pay period. Multi-State Tax and Compliance Specialty contractors operating across state lines must withhold and remit taxes correctly for each state where work is performed. State income tax rules, unemployment insurance rates, and workers' compensation requirements vary significantly. A payroll platform that defaults to the contractor's home state and requires manual adjustments for every out-of-state project is not built for multi-state operations. Trade Classifications and Pay Rate Management Construction workers are not paid a single hourly rate. A journeyman electrician on a prevailing wage project in New York earns a different rate than the same worker on a private project in New Jersey. The payroll system must manage multiple pay rates per worker based on trade classification, project type, and jurisdiction, and apply the correct rate automatically based on the work assignment. Where Most Payroll Platforms Fall Short The construction payroll software market includes three broad categories, and each one has a characteristic gap. General-Purpose Payroll Providers Large payroll providers serve millions of businesses across every industry. The core product handles direct deposit, tax filings, and basic reporting well. The limitation is that construction-specific workflows, including prevailing wage, union logic, certified payroll, and project-level cost tracking, are either unsupported or available only through add-on modules that do not integrate deeply with the core payroll engine. Contractors using these platforms typically maintain parallel spreadsheets for prevailing wage calculations and assemble certified payroll filings manually. Legacy Construction Accounting Platforms Established construction accounting systems have handled job costing and payroll for decades. Many offer prevailing wage and union payroll capabilities built over years of industry-specific development. The tradeoff is that these platforms were designed around desktop software architectures. Field connectivity is limited, mobile access is often an afterthought, and the user experience reflects design decisions made fifteen or twenty years ago. Payroll data entry still depends heavily on the back office rather than flowing from the field. Standalone Time-Tracking Tools With Payroll Features Several construction technology companies offer field time tracking with a payroll layer on top. The time-tracking component may be strong, capturing GPS-verified clock-ins, cost code tagging, and daily logs. The payroll side, however, often lacks the depth needed for prevailing wage calculations, certified payroll generation, union reporting, and multi-state compliance. Contractors outgrow these tools the moment they take on a Davis-Bacon project or start working across state lines. How to Evaluate Construction Payroll Software A construction payroll software comparison should test against the hardest scenarios your operation faces, not the simplest ones. Can the platform handle prevailing wage payroll natively? Ask the vendor to demonstrate a prevailing wage payroll run with split classifications, fringe benefit calculations, and certified payroll output. If the process requires exporting data to a separate tool, manually adjusting rates, or assembling the WH-347 outside the platform, prevailing wage support is not native. Genuine support means the wage determination, fringe calculation, and certified payroll filing are all handled within the same system. Does payroll pull data from the field automatically? The best construction payroll platforms in 2026 do not start the payroll process with manual data entry. Hours, cost codes, and trade classifications captured in the field through daily shift reports should flow directly into the payroll engine. If the admin team is still transcribing paper timesheets or importing CSV files from a separate time-tracking tool, the payroll process has a data gap that introduces errors every cycle. How does the platform handle union payroll complexity? Different trades on the same project may have different CBA-driven pay rules. Ask whether the platform can manage multiple union agreements simultaneously, calculate trade-specific benefit fund contributions, apply CBA overtime triggers that differ from federal or state rules, and generate the union reporting that your fund administrators require. Does payroll connect to job costing? Payroll data that does not flow into job costing means the project management team is working with labor cost estimates instead of actuals. When payroll and job costing share the same system, every paid hour is automatically assigned to a project, phase, and cost code. Burn rates and spend-to-date figures update with each payroll cycle. Can the platform scale with multi-state growth? A contractor operating in two states today may be in five states next year. Ask whether the platform handles state tax registration, jurisdiction-specific withholding rules, and state prevailing wage requirements without manual configuration for each new state. The payroll system should adapt to new jurisdictions as the business grows, not require a rebuild every time a project crosses a state line. What to Look for Beyond Payroll Construction payroll does not operate in isolation. The best construction payroll software connects to the upstream and downstream functions that depend on the same data. Integration With HR and Onboarding When a new worker completes onboarding , their trade classification, tax information, and benefits enrollment should populate the payroll system automatically. Manual data transfer between HR and payroll is where classification errors and pay rate mismatches originate. Reporting and Compliance Output Beyond certified payroll, contractors need payroll reporting that supports union fund remittance reports, workers' compensation audits, multi-state tax filings, and project-level labor cost breakdowns. Evaluate the platform's reporting capabilities against the specific filings your operation produces regularly. Field Connectivity A payroll platform that depends on the back office to enter every hour worked is a platform that scales only as fast as the admin team can type. Direct field-to-payroll data flow through a foreman or worker app is what separates construction payroll software from general payroll tools with a construction label. Choosing the Right Platform for Your Operation The right construction payroll software eliminates the gap between field operations and the back office. For specialty trade contractors, that means a platform where prevailing wage, union logic, multi-state compliance, and certified payroll are built into the core system, not bolted on as afterthoughts. Trayd's construction payroll engine is purpose-built for specialty trade contractors running union labor, prevailing wage projects, and multi-state crews. Payroll pulls directly from field data, applies the correct rates and rules by project, and generates certified payroll and compliance reports without manual assembly. Book a demo to see how it handles your most complex pay period. Frequently Asked Questions What makes construction payroll software different from regular payroll software? Construction payroll must handle trade classifications with multiple pay rates per worker, prevailing wage determinations, union benefit fund contributions, certified payroll reporting, project-level cost allocation, and multi-state tax compliance. Regular payroll software is not built for these workflows. Do I need separate software for certified payroll? Not if the payroll platform handles prevailing wage natively. A well-built construction payroll system generates certified payroll reports (Form WH-347) directly from the same data used to run payroll, without exporting to a separate tool. How should I evaluate construction payroll software for union work? Test whether the platform manages multiple collective bargaining agreements simultaneously, calculates trade-specific benefit fund contributions, applies CBA-driven overtime triggers, and produces union reporting. Manual overrides for every union-specific rule are a sign the system lacks native support. Can construction payroll software handle multiple states? The right platform manages state-specific tax withholding, unemployment insurance, workers' compensation, and prevailing wage requirements by jurisdiction. Ask whether adding a new state requires manual configuration or is handled natively as projects are created. What is the most important integration for construction payroll? Field-to-payroll data flow. When hours, cost codes, and trade classifications captured at the jobsite feed directly into the payroll engine, the admin team reviews data instead of assembling it. Manual hour entry is the biggest source of payroll errors and processing delays. How much does construction payroll software typically cost? Pricing varies widely based on company size, feature set, and whether compliance modules are included or sold separately. Ask vendors for transparent pricing that includes prevailing wage, certified payroll, and union payroll capabilities rather than quoting a base price with add-on fees.

title: Weekly Investment Perspective July 14, 2026
summary: U.S. equities finished the week broadly higher, though the gains masked a volatile ride driven by renewed hostilities in the Middle East.
body_text: Blog Detail U.S. equities finished the week broadly higher, though the gains masked a volatile ride driven by renewed hostilities in the Middle East. The Nasdaq Composite led with a 1.74% gain, while the S&P 500 advanced 1.23%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.50%, and the small-cap Russell 2000 fell 0.61%. Growth stocks once again outpaced value, with information technology leading sector performance while materials and health care were among the weakest performers. The week also highlighted just how volatile the AI trade has become after powering much of the market’s first-half advance. Semiconductor stocks swung sharply throughout the week as investors rotated in and out of many of the year’s strongest performers before technology ultimately regained its footing. Nvidia and Meta helped lead the rebound, reinforcing that enthusiasm surrounding AI infrastructure spending remains the market’s primary source of leadership despite periodic bouts of profit taking. Geopolitical risks returned to the forefront after President Trump declared that the June ceasefire agreement with Iran was “over,” following renewed military exchanges centered around the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. carried out additional strikes targeting Iranian air defense systems, missile facilities, and coastal radar sites, while Iran responded with attacks against U.S. military installations across several Gulf states. Although the latest flare-up has increased uncertainty and pushed oil prices higher, markets have so far remained relatively measured. Investors have now witnessed several rounds of escalation followed by renewed diplomatic engagement, limiting expectations that the conflict will broaden into a more sustained regional conflict. Even so, the Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint given that roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies transit the waterway. Higher energy prices are also beginning to weigh on demand, with the International Energy Agency now forecasting that global oil demand will decline in 2026, marking the first annual contraction outside of the pandemic and suggesting early signs of demand destruction. Last week’s Federal Reserve minutes reinforced that policymakers remain divided on the appropriate path for interest rates as they navigate an economy that continues to grow while inflation remains above the Fed’s target. Some participants indicated policy rates could finish the year modestly below current levels if inflation continues to improve, while others argued that persistent price pressures could ultimately require tighter policy. For investors, the broader message changed little as the Fed continues to emphasize a patient, data-dependent approach under new Chair Kevin Warsh rather than signaling an imminent shift in policy. This week’s inflation data will therefore take on added importance as markets continue to debate the direction of monetary policy. The AI investment cycle also remained a dominant market theme. South Korea’s SK Hynix, one of the world’s largest producers of advanced memory chips used in AI servers, made its U.S. trading debut last week with a strong reception as its Nasdaq-listed shares rose 13% on the first day of trading. The listing raised $26.5 billion, the largest U.S. listing ever by a foreign company, underscoring continued investor enthusiasm for companies tied to AI infrastructure. At the same time, U.S. bond markets are absorbing a surge in debt issuance tied to the AI infrastructure buildout, with large tech companies raising more than $360 billion in AI related issuance over the past twelve months alone. The pace of capital raising, and the market’s ability to absorb it, has become an increasingly important barometer of investor risk appetite as the AI infrastructure buildout enters an even more capital-intensive phase. Looking ahead, investors will first focus on Tuesday’s June Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, the final major inflation reading before the Federal Reserve’s late-July policy meeting. Consensus expectations call for headline inflation to moderate to 3.8% year-over-year from 4.2% in May, while core inflation is expected to remain at 2.9%. Markets will also closely watch Chair Kevin Warsh’s first semiannual testimony before Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday for any additional insight into how the Fed is balancing resilient economic growth against lingering inflation pressures. Retail sales, industrial production, and consumer sentiment later in the week will provide additional clues on the health of the U.S. economy. Second-quarter earnings season also begins in earnest this week with reports from JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, and Morgan Stanley, followed later by Johnson & Johnson, Netflix, GE Aerospace, and several other bellwether companies. Analysts currently expect S&P 500 companies to deliver roughly 24% year-over-year earnings growth, which would represent one of the strongest quarters of profit growth in several years. While geopolitical developments and inflation data may drive near term volatility, the combination of solid earnings expectations, resilient economic activity, and continued investment in AI infrastructure remains supportive of the broader market backdrop. 2026 The Long View | First Merchants Bank Index YTD Total Returns S&P 500 Index 11.36% Dow Jones Industrial Average 10.46% NASDAQ Index 13.44% S&P 400 Mid Cap Index 15.16% S&P 600 Small Cap Index 21.58% Russell 2000 Small Cap Index 20.71% MSCI All Country World ex-USA 13.73% Bloomberg Barclays US Aggregate (TR) 0.04% Returns are through | 7/10/2026

title: Coleman® and Kane Brown Celebrate Multi-Year Partnership with the Launch of Limited-Edition Collection
summary: Coleman's First-Ever Music Partnership Brings Kane Brown's Signature Style to Summer's Outdoor Must-Haves Coleman® launches the limited-edition Coleman x Kane Brown Collection, the debut release from the brand's first-ever music partnership and multi-year collaboration with the global superstar
body_text: Coleman's First-Ever Music Partnership Brings Kane Brown's Signature Style to Summer's Outdoor Must-Haves Coleman® launches the limited-edition Coleman x Kane Brown Collection, the debut release from the brand's first-ever music partnership and multi-year collaboration with the global superstar Inspired by Brown's life on tour and love of the outdoors, the collection brings his signature style to a Steel-Belted Hard Cooler, Soft Cooler Sling, Stainless-Steel Tumbler and upcoming Snap 'N Go™ Hard Collapsible Cooler Multi-year collaboration unites outdoor recreation, music and fan experiences through future product launches, content and activations ATLANTA , July 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, Coleman® and Kane Brown announced the launch of the limited-edition Coleman x Kane Brown Collection, the debut release from the brand's first-ever music partnership and long-term collaboration with award-winning, multi-platinum country global superstar Kane Brown. Inspired by Brown's life on tour, love for the outdoors, and favorite summer traditions, the collection features a custom Steel-Belted Hard Cooler, Soft Cooler Sling, and Stainless-Steel Tumbler, with a Snap 'N Go™ Hard Collapsible Cooler arriving later this year. Reimagining Coleman classics through Brown's signature style, the limited-edition collection offers fans a collectible take on outdoor essentials featuring Kane-inspired design details and his signature "KB" branding. A longtime outdoorsman, Brown has incorporated Coleman products into both his personal life and professional life on the road. The collaboration builds on Coleman's sponsorship of The High Road Tour , where Coleman gear traveled alongside Brown and his crew, appearing backstage and helping power the moments between performances. As Coleman's official ambassador, Brown will influence product development and activations while introducing the brand to new audiences across music, culture, and lifestyle. "I love the line I was able to create with Coleman," said Kane Brown. "From the cups that we use on stage every night to toast the fans to the limited-edition Snap 'N Go cooler, coming this Fall. I have really enjoyed working with the Coleman team on this collection and showing fans the products I use at my home, on the road, and at the beach. I hope everyone enjoys them as much as I do." "As our first country music brand ambassador, Kane embodies our brand purpose by inspiring the next generation to forge their own outdoor traditions," said Jimmy Jia, Global Vice President of Brand Management, Outdoor & Recreation at Newell Brands. "From tailgates to backyard parties to life on the road with his crew, he uses our products in authentic ways every day. Together, we've created an exclusive capsule that reflects Coleman and Kane's distinct trailblazing style." Kane Brown's Summer Essentials The inaugural Coleman x Kane Brown Collection features a Steel-Belted Hard Cooler, Soft Cooler Sling, and Stainless-Steel Tumbler, with a Snap 'N Go™ Hard Collapsible Cooler arriving later this year. Drawing inspiration from tailgates before shows, beach trips with family, and life on tour, Brown helped shape the collection's colors, graphics, and product selections to reflect how he spends his time outdoors. Each piece features unique colorways and design details personally selected by Brown, complete with his iconic "KB" logo or signature, offering fans functional outdoor essentials inspired by his life both on the road and at home. Kane's Steel-Belted Hard Cooler: Durable steel cooler with 4-day ice retention, 85-can capacity, and built-in bottle opener, featuring Kane's etched signature ($239.99) Kane's Soft Cooler Sling: Hands-free cooler bag with adjustable sling, 6-can capacity, and 12+ hours of cooling, featuring Kane's iconic "KB" logo ($21.99) Kane's Stainless-Steel Tumbler : Vacuum-insulated 20oz tumbler that keeps drinks cold for 18 hours or hot for 6 hours, featuring an iridescent finish, sweatproof design and splash-resistant lid, and iconic "KB" logo ($34.99) Coming Soon: Kane's Snap 'N Go Hard Collapsible Cooler: Portable 45QT collapsible cooler, with 2-day ice retention, 76-can capacity, that folds to one-third its size, complete with exclusive Kane Brown typography ($229.99). Visit Coleman.com today to sign-up for launch updates. The limited-edition Coleman x Kane Brown Collection will be available beginning July 22, 2026, while supplies last on Coleman.com . An Exclusive First Look To celebrate the launch, Coleman and Brown hosted an exclusive preview event at Kane Brown's Broadway bar in Nashville, where guests received an immersive first look at the limited-edition collection through hands-on product experiences and outdoor-inspired activations. Attendees included Brown's friends and family, who joined him in raising a toast to the collaboration ahead of its official debut. The Next Chapter of Coleman x Kane Brown The collection marks the first chapter of Coleman and Brown's broader multi-year collaboration, which will continue to bring together outdoor recreation, music, and fan engagement through future products, experiences, and content. Later this year, the collection will expand with a highly anticipated custom Kane Brown-inspired Snap 'N Go™ cooler. Fans are invited to sign up for launch updates now on Coleman.com . For more information, visit Coleman.com or follow @ColemanUSA on social media. And to keep up with Kane Brown, follow INSTAGRAM , TIKTOK , and FACEBOOK . ABOUT COLEMAN For over 120 years, The Coleman Company, Inc. has been a trusted partner for unforgettable moments outside. Whether you're cheering on your team or enjoying a cookout with friends, Coleman makes every outdoor adventure more memorable. We believe that the joy of outdoor gatherings brings people closer together—strengthening bonds and creating lasting memories. To learn more, visit coleman.com and follow us on Instagram . ABOUT NEWELL BRANDS Newell Brands (NASDAQ: NWL) is a leading global consumer goods company with a strong portfolio of well-known brands, including Rubbermaid, Sharpie®, Graco®, Coleman®, Rubbermaid Commercial Products®, Yankee Candle®, Paper Mate®, FoodSaver®, Dymo®, EXPO®, Elmer's®, Oster®, NUK®, Spontex® and Campingaz®. Newell Brands is focused on delighting consumers by lighting up everyday moments. ABOUT KANE BROWN: Named "the future of country music" (Billboard), Multi-Platinum-selling, award-winning singer/songwriter Kane Brown "didn't fit the country music mold. So he made his own." (The New York Times). Kicking off 2026 strong, Brown just released his song "Woman," which follows the success of his widely acclaimed 2025 record, The High Road . Listen to the song HERE . Brown first broke onto the scene with the arrival of his self-titled, 2X Platinum debut album (2016), where he became the first artist ever to lead all five of Billboard's main country charts simultaneously and topped the Billboard Top Country Albums chart for more than 13 weeks and earned two of the most-streamed country songs of all time (chart-topping singles Diamond Certified "Heaven," and "What Ifs"). His album Experiment (2018) hit #1 on the Billboard Top 200 all genre list-becoming the first Country artist in more than 24 years to top the chart with a sophomore album. Brown released his multi-song project Mixtape Vol. 1- which earned Brown an ACM Award nomination for Album of the Year (2021) and an ACM win for "Video of the Year." Expanding beyond music, Brown has stepped into film and television, guest starring on 9-1-1: Nashville , and serving as executive producer on Thank God: Christmas at Keller Ranch . He is also the founder of Verse2, a publishing venture in partnership with Sony Music Publishing, further solidifying his growing influence across the industry. This summer, Brown also opened his new Nashville bar, Kane Brown's On Broadway, marking his latest entrepreneurial venture and expansion in Music City. Named to Time's 100 most influential people in the world (2021), Kane Brown has ascended from independently built social media notability to an ACM Entertainer of the Year nominee (2023 & 2024) - and has become one of country music's most accomplished mainstays and global entertainers. With 13 chart-topping No. 1 singles at Country radio, internationally sold out tours and stadium dates, Brown continues to garner a series of milestones that continue to expand the perception of country music and break musical boundaries- from being named to the Time100 list (2021) to becoming the first black artist in history to headline and sell out Boston's historic Fenway Park (2023) to his win ACM Video of the Year (2021) and multiple ACM, Billboard, AMA, CMT and People's Choice Award nominations, including most recently, his recognition by the People's Choice Country Awards with a Country Champion Award win. Brown has also earned numerous accolades for his ongoing work with The Boys & Girls Club, including the Country Radio Seminar (CRS) Humanitarian Award and the Champion of Youth Award from The Boys & Girls Club.
